note: Adapted from the species-level description (Soldier, fig. 18) and TABLE 15 in Krishna & Araujo's revision of the genus Neocapritermes (Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History, vol. 138), the original in English; only the soldier caste is treated. The description of this species is not contained in its own pack: that pack (_tmp/ia_pack2/neocapritermes-talpa.txt) holds only the key to the genus Neocapritermes, Holmgren's 1906 ecological account and the full description of the closely related N. angusticeps, while the complete treatment of this species falls in the N. parvus pack of the same work and the same batch (_tmp/ia_pack2/neocapritermes-parvus.txt), lines 276—540, and was therefore taken across packs. The synonymy list includes Capritermes talpa Holmgren, 1906 and Neocapritermes hopkinsi Snyder, 1924.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow; the anterior margin of the head, the antennae and the margins of the postmentum tinged with brown; labrum pale yellow; thoracic tergites and legs yellow; abdomen dirty white; mandibles shiny black. Head with sparse, fairly long, almost colourless erect bristles on the dorsum and the sides, very few ventrally; the distal half of the postmentum has only very few bristles; thoracic tergites with sparse erect bristles; legs almost hairless, only the distal 2/3 of the tibiae with a few long fine bristles, the mid tibiae with numerous short stout bristles, the longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa with a row of bristles and a few more on the inner side; abdomen with numerous bristles of two lengths. Head elongate, twice as long as wide and 1.6 times as long as the left mandible, sides parallel, the anterolateral corner below the antennal fossa slightly swollen; posterior 1/4 gently rounded and passing into a straight posterior margin; in dorsal view the top is straight, its distal 1/3 gently sloping towards the frons, the posterior margin rounded, the venter broadly concave; the postclypeal area is almost undistorted, its anterior margin concave, the left side extremely slightly raised; fontanelle minute, lying in a very small pit. Antennae 16-segmented, segment 4 the shortest, extremely slightly shorter than segment 3, segments 5—10 progressively longer, segments 11 and 12 as long as segment 10, segments 13—15 equal, segment 16 oval-elongate and extremely slightly longer than segment 15. Labrum relatively small, almost undistorted, the left side slightly concave, the right side straight or slightly convex, the anterior margin extremely shallowly concave, with small lateral lobes. Mandibles very stout, the left extremely slightly longer than the right. In lateral view the left mandible is bent at a right angle at about the proximal 1/3 and tapers towards the club-shaped tip; in dorsal view the bend is wider than the postclypeus, tapering extremely gently towards the tip. The right mandible is more strongly curved in lateral view; in dorsal view it has a shallow groove along the dorsum, the inner margin with tooth-like projections, and the tip drawn out into a fairly long sharp point. The postmentum is nearly parallel-sided over most of its length, widening over the distal 1/6, the sides straight and converging towards the anterior margin; at the base the sides diverge proximally; the posterior margin almost straight. Pronotum 0.6 of the head width, the anterior and posterior lobes at an angle of 45 degrees; the anterior lobe 1/3 shorter than the posterior lobe; the anterior margin a very broad arc with a shallow median notch; the anterior corners of the posterior lobe rounded, the sides almost straight, converging towards the straight posterior margin. Mesonotum transverse, 0.6 as long as wide, the posterior margin straight, the sides rounded. Metanotum slightly wider than the pronotum, with a transverse median notch distally, the sides arched over nearly half their length, the posterior margin broadly, shallowly and evenly concave. Mid tibiae with numerous (5 or 6) short spine-like bristles. Measurements (7 soldiers; the three columns in the original are, in order, syntype, range and mean): head capsule length in lateral view 3.72 mm, 3.06—3.72 mm, 3.29 mm; maximum head width 1.89 mm, 1.63—1.89 mm, 1.76 mm; maximum head height 1.61 mm, 1.43—1.66 mm, 1.54 mm; left mandible length 2.35 mm, 2.04—2.35 mm, 2.21 mm; right mandible length 2.04 mm, 1.79—2.04 mm, 1.92 mm; postmentum maximum width 0.61 mm, 0.51—0.61 mm, 0.56 mm; postmentum minimum width 0.27 mm, 0.24—0.31 mm, 0.28 mm; postmentum length 3.06 mm, 2.30—3.06 mm, 2.51 mm; pronotum median length 0.59 mm, 0.51—0.61 mm, 0.56 mm; pronotum maximum length 0.66 mm, 0.56—0.66 mm, 0.62 mm; pronotum maximum width 1.17 mm, 1.02—1.17 mm, 1.09 mm; hind tibia length 1.48 mm, 1.25—1.48 mm, 1.33 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The very broad and strongly twisted left mandible of the soldier groups this species with N. talpoides and N. guyana. N. talpoides has all measurements smaller, the bend in the middle of the left mandible less strong, the postmentum more projecting in lateral view, the anterior margin of the labrum asymmetrically narrowed, the fore coxa with only very few small hard bristles, the anterior and posterior lobes of the pronotum equal in length, the median notch of the anterior margin narrower and deeper, and the sides of the posterior lobe evenly and gently rounded. N. guyana has all measurements much smaller, the labrum with only 1 apical lobe and convex sides, the anterior lobe of the pronotum about as long as the posterior lobe, the median notch of the anterior margin deeper, and the metanotum very broad and deeply concave.
